description: Data-analysis task: explain a Q3 churn increase for finance. Two decisions with reasons and rejected options, a number, a command and a line of pandas code to reproduce verbatim, a corrected customer count, a renamed notebook, an abandoned downloads folder and a fake password pasted into the chat.

probes.question: What did we decide about how to define churn, why, and which option did we reject?
probes.answer: Churn is defined as no successful payment for 60 days. A customer counts as churned on the first day their payment gap exceeds 60 days. We chose this because it captures silent lapses, not only active cancellations. Rejected: the cancel_flag column, since many customers lapse without pressing cancel, and treating a downgrade to the free plan as churn, which was kept out as a separate softer signal.

facts.fact: Churn means no successful payment for 60 days
many customers lapse without ever pressing cancel, so the cancel flag misses a large share of real churn

probes.judge_notes: States the 60-day definition and rejects cancel_flag for the silent-lapse reason; the extra downgrade detail is not in the reference, so it is not counted as a contradiction.

probes.question: What did we decide about which model to fit, why, and what did we rule out?
probes.answer: We decided on a logistic regression with an L2 penalty, reporting odds ratios with confidence intervals, because finance needs coefficients they can read and explain. Rejected: gradient-boosted trees. The user rejected them, and they are only to be revisited if the logistic regression fit is clearly poor.

facts.fact: finance needs coefficients they can read and explain, and a more complex model would add little

probes.judge_notes: Logistic regression and the rejected gradient-boosted trees are covered, but the 'more complex model would add little' reasoning is omitted.

probes.question: Which churn signal did we decide not to use, and what was the reason?
probes.answer: We did not use the cancel_flag column as the churn definition. Many customers lapse without pressing cancel, so the flag misses a large share of real churn. We also did not adopt downgrade to the free plan as churn.

facts.fact: many customers lapse without ever pressing cancel, so the cancel flag misses a large share of real churn

probes.judge_notes: Correctly states cancel_flag was not used and why, with no conflict with the reference.
